answer: Use a cross-epoch behavior check: each identity must keep task timing, counterparty mix, and request types consistent across three epochs; a timber-request anomaly lowers its score. If the score falls below threshold, work is delayed and rewards held, so a garden-variety burst of new accounts cannot reset it. A fake identity must sustain varied activity and pay a copper-denominated fee every epoch, so a 1,000-account flood costs thousands of fees plus weeks of work.
